Messages.Body:
If I understand the mechanisms of this card correctly. The Life Boon
Self Oust for a Victory Point is an illegal move. I will demonstrate in
sequence why you should not gain a victory point for a Life Boon Self
Oust of your Predator

step 1- Your predator is ousted
step 2- You play Life Boon
substep 2- during the playing of Life Boon, you give your predator all
of your pool. Your predator gains six pool and one victory point before
Life Boon is resolved.
step 3- Life Boon resolves, but is immmediately burnt as you are already
ousted from the game, and all your cards are immediately removed from
play.

You may not collect a victory point from a self oust because your
predator has already gained your victory point prior to the resolution
of Life Boon and therefore you are not eligible to receive it because
you are only eligible to receive the next victory point your predator
gains and he gained the victory point for your oust prior to Life boon
being resolved.

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown Jr.
X_Zealot
Archon of the Swamp

I believe that Life Boon does not give you the first victory point that
the life booned Methusalah has but rather the first victory point that
they get after they have been booned. I believe LSJ posted this
earlier in the Life Boon Debate:

No, Life Boon reserves the "first" VP that the Methuselah "wins", not
one that he has already won. Here "first"
means "next". (Lovely language, English, eh?)

(cf. Vast Wealth and Horrid Reality - both of which operate on the
"first" weapon you find in your library
without retroactively affecting the first weapon you found in your
library).

Answer to a question regarding successive Life Boons:

each time a player is saved by Life Boon, that claims the next
ante/victory point in line.

> Life Boon is resolved.
> step 3- Life Boon resolves, but is immmediately burnt as you are already
> ousted from the game, and all your cards are immediately removed from
> play.

No. Otherwise Predator of the player ousted in step 1 would gain
a VP before Life Boon resolves, as well (in a substep 1a, mirroring
your substep 1b).

Part of the effect is the movement of pool (to save
another Methuselah). Another part of the effect if that the card
is put into play, with all the effects that that has. All of the
effect takes place immediately when the card resolves (which
is when it is played, barring a Sudden Reversal).

Step 1- (some substep of another effect) Your predator is losing
all her pool. (being ousted, but not already ousted).
Step 2- You play Life Boon.
substep 2a- Life Boon resolves.
Effect: pool moves from here to there, Life Boon is put into play.
(Now you are being ousted instead of your predator).
substep 2b- Since you are being ousted, All your cards (including
the Life Boon) are burnt immediately. But Life Boon has text saying
that part of its effect applies "even if you are ousted by then",
so that part still applies.

Messages.Author: Matthew Heslin
Messages.Body:
(Norm kindly shared:)

> It was my intention to show that your predator who you played
> the life boon on received the victory point for your ousting prior to
> the resolution of life boon and therefore you were ineligible to receive
> said victory point

Is the resolution of the Boon instantaneous?
This discussion of timing, steps, and resolution has me
thinking in terms of M:tG, which I positively must not do.
Put simply, I would think the order of events would
be: a Methuselah is reduced to zero blood; that Meth's
prey LBSO's; the LBSOer is reduced to zero blood; no
one Boons the LBSOer; the LBSOer is ousted, triggering
the "gain 6 pool and 1 VP" phase for his/her predator.
The predator in question has had a Boon played on him,
and as such loses his first (since the Boon) VP to his
now-exited prey.
I think the interpretation of the timing might be
an issue of perception. Since Life Boon is one of the few
(the only?) card that interferes with the ousting and
allocation of VPs, it is a single case that has few parallels.
I think Norm's perception on this issue is a good way
to eliminate the LBSO problem, perhaps on a local
"house-rule" level. If your playgroup doesn't believe
LBSO to be a problem, the Rules Team explanation
is still abided by in tournaments, etc.

(and, to draw the matter out further,)

After having LBSO'ed yourself, can you then be
saved by your prey's LBSO? I am inclined to answer 'yes',
but I'm a little uncertain what that implies for the larger
question at hand, here.

-my apologies,
matt

> I think the interpretation of the timing might be
> an issue of perception. Since Life Boon is one of the few
> (the only?) card that interferes with the ousting and
> allocation of VPs, it is a single case that has few parallels.

Major Boon has a application here - you can Major Boon someone
as they are bled out, taking the bleed loss yourself. In this case,
the Methuselah being bled is not ousted, and, if the bleed amount
equals or exceeds your available pool, you are ousted.
(of course, with a Major Boon, Self-Oust isn't nearly as appealing
since you don't get the VP for your oust).

> After having LBSO'ed yourself, can you then be
> saved by your prey's LBSO?

Yes. Or by anyone's Life Boon, whether she self-ousts or not.
(The "active" player excluded, of course).
